The ACC/AHA report suggests that given the current average intake of saturated fat at 11 
percent, it would be beneficial to decrease saturated fat intake to 5 to 6 percent of calories for those 
who need to lower LDL-C levels.
Saturated fatty acids, when contrasted with unsaturated fatty acids, decrease synthesis and activ­
ity of LDL-C receptors, promoting an increase in serum LDL-C, thereby contributing to athero­
genesis. An increase of 1 mg/dL in serum LDL-C increases CHD risk by 1 percent. A meta-analysis 
of dietary studies concluded that for every 1 percent increase in calories from saturated fat, serum 
LDL-C increases approximately 2 percent. Consuming a diet rich in vegetables, fruits, low-fat dairy
